topics.name: Software and GUI Agents
topics.summary: GUI and software agents are assessed through accessibility-grounded actions, dynamic tool protocols, executable repository tasks, and evidence-gated workflows. Results favor typed or structured execution with verification and recovery over unconstrained clicking or fluent completion claims.

topics.name: Agent Evaluation and Verification
topics.summary: Agent benchmarks increasingly measure critique uptake, escalation, resource use, reproducibility, and evidence quality alongside task success. Interactive security, mathematical reasoning, and game-like environments show that reliable completion requires observable actions and recovery from failure.

topics.name: Agentic Scientific Reasoning and Evidence Synthesis
topics.summary: Scientific agents combine structured planning, causal decomposition, topology-aware reasoning, specialist retrieval, and evidence screening. Their evaluations emphasize inspectable intermediate decisions and useful document selection rather than answers produced without a trace.

topics.name: Security of AI Agents and ML Infrastructure
topics.summary: Security analyses cover structural monitoring for code agents, persistent memory poisoning, malicious setup instructions, training-data manipulation, and federated-learning fingerprinting. Across these settings, hidden dependencies and delayed effects make pipeline-wide monitoring more important than payload inspection alone.

topics.name: Vision-Language-Action Navigation and World Models
topics.summary: Embodied policies improve through 3D scene tokens, action-conditioned prediction, visual foresight, streaming inference, long-context histories, and test-time adaptation. Navigation, aerial flight, and manipulation studies report better transfer and closed-loop control when future state is modeled explicitly.

topics.name: Robot Safety and Policy Assurance
topics.summary: Robot safety studies combine active policy testing, acceleration-based and belief-space barrier constraints, formal policy synthesis, and representation-level risk probes. Simulated and physical evaluations show that explicit violation controls are needed when learned behavior faces perturbations, crowds, or hazardous actions.

topics.name: Robot Motion Planning and Multi-Robot Coordination
topics.summary: Planning systems use constrained diffusion, flow matching, curvature-aware arrival laws, relative-pose communication, and kinodynamic optimization. The recurring goal is fast, feasible motion under collision, topology, speed, and communication constraints in manipulation, driving, and multi-robot settings.

topics.name: Robotic Manipulation and Tactile Sensing
topics.summary: Manipulation research pairs compliant or shape-adaptive hardware with torque, tactile, haptic, and contact-aligned representations. Agricultural harvesting, insertion, in-hand tracking, and dexterous grasping results indicate that sensing future contact consequences improves robustness beyond vision-only control.

topics.name: Humanoid and Assistive Human-Robot Interaction
topics.summary: Whole-body humanoid control, anticipatory teleoperation, social-robot assessment, and risk-sensitive preference learning address physical interaction with uncertain human timing or goals. The studies favor predictive assistance and measurable safety feedback over purely reactive control.

topics.name: Multimodal Spatial Grounding
topics.summary: Spatially grounded multimodal systems combine ego-scene structure, cross-level visual priors, audio-visual correspondence, geolocation evidence, and part-level 3D cues. These additions improve localization and spatial question answering when a single salient object or landmark is misleading.

topics.name: Domain-Specific Multimodal Reasoning
topics.summary: Benchmarks for scientific figures, repository issues, construction drawings, editable diagrams, virtual-reality behavior, and harmful memes test whether models use domain structure and interaction evidence. Performance gaps persist when systems rely on surface text instead of quantitative, temporal, or social interpretation.

topics.name: Language-Model Evaluation and Uncertainty
topics.summary: Evaluation studies examine language-sensitive judging, logical reformulations, perturbation choices, rubric quality, item-response models, and deployment-consistent inputs. They show that score changes can reflect evaluator language, protocol design, or uncertainty artifacts rather than genuine capability differences.

topics.name: AI Governance and Fairness
topics.summary: Governance work combines public-preference surveys, subgroup privacy audits, fairness interventions, and cross-national responsible-AI indicators. The findings support context-specific oversight because aggregate performance and universal policy templates can hide unequal effects or conflicting social priorities.

topics.name: Causal and Counterfactual Machine Learning
topics.summary: Causal and counterfactual analyses use gradient-based fairness objectives, feature-weighted clustering, covariate interventions, and sequential causal models. Their common finding is that useful explanations and equitable decisions depend on structural assumptions rather than isolated feature rankings.

topics.name: AI-Generated Content Integrity
topics.summary: Content-integrity methods inspect internal geometry, reasoning graphs, ordered embedding changes, caption consistency, and transferable detector attacks. Results show that authorship and deepfake judgments remain vulnerable to paraphrase, cross-model shifts, and systematic image-text mismatch.

topics.name: Human-AI Creative Authorship
topics.summary: Empirical studies of AI-assisted art and writing compare self-reported contribution, perceived ownership, intent, and machine involvement. They find that numerical attribution schemes do not fully capture how creators understand agency and responsibility.

topics.name: Controllable Image Generation
topics.summary: Image-generation systems use counterfactual concepts, attention regulation, negative prompting, classifier guidance, and frequency-aware objectives to alter content while preserving detail. Applications include rare attributes, safer outputs, demographic coverage, and mask-free virtual try-on.

topics.name: Video Generation, Editing, and Streaming
topics.summary: Video systems improve practicality through autoregressive shot selection, prompt adaptation, structured reference binding, causal decoding, one-step object removal, persistent scene memory, and hierarchical denoising. The recurring tradeoff is preserving temporal coherence while reducing latency, memory, or sampling cost.

topics.name: Efficient and Robust Video Perception
topics.summary: Video-perception studies use efficient temporal attention, event timing, weak labels, panoramic memory, pseudo-annotations, patch motion cues, and bandwidth-aware keypoints. Applications span crop monitoring, aerial tracking, camera health, fall detection, salient-object segmentation, and generated-video detection.

topics.name: 3D Gaussian Reconstruction and Mapping
topics.summary: Geometric matching, global consistency, GPU-friendly texture coding, object-level semantic correspondence, adaptive road-surface representations, and event-based reconstruction support scalable 3D mapping. These methods target unordered captures, changing scenes, large areas, and sensor-induced drift.

topics.name: Geometric Registration and Shape Deformation
topics.summary: Registration and shape-editing methods use Hough-space structure, rectified-flow LiDAR densification, tangent-space guidance, learned deformation priors, and phase-error correction. The shared aim is stable correspondence or nonrigid transformation under occlusion, noise, motion, and semantic constraints.

topics.name: Computational Imaging and Learned Reconstruction
topics.summary: Learned priors are combined with proximal adaptation, Fourier-local fields, event-assisted sensing, and structured optical coding to recover images or geometry from indirect measurements. The studies balance reconstruction fidelity against acquisition complexity, memory, and domain mismatch.

topics.name: Medical Imaging Representation Learning
topics.summary: Medical vision systems use multimodal language supervision, pathology-slide teacher ensembles, semantic contrastive objectives, parameter-efficient prompting, information-based MRI selection, quantization, and foundation-model patch tokens. These approaches seek clinically useful predictions when labels, memory, or input sequences are limited.

topics.name: Clinical Multimodal Models and Health Analytics
topics.summary: Clinical AI studies align narrative events with physiological time series, combine multimodal patient records, and build transparent risk or resource-allocation models. ICU prediction, medical safety annotation, emergency bed planning, and population vulnerability analyses emphasize calibration and evidence quality.

topics.name: Biomedical and Wearable Biosignal Learning
topics.summary: Biosignal systems separate person-specific and task-specific information, use angular or low-power representations, and test robustness to missing sensors and demographic variation. Applications include surface EMG, arrhythmia screening, sleep-apnea detection, and EEG-gated assistive control.

topics.name: Affective, Audio, and Social State Modeling
topics.summary: Audio-visual models combine speech, facial cues, scene context, infrared signals, and dialogue structure for emotion, ambivalence, personality, and driver-state recognition. Speaker verification and emotion-aware summarization further show that vocal dynamics carry information absent from transcripts alone.

topics.name: Accessible Multimodal Interfaces
topics.summary: Accessibility systems support blind and low-vision users through visual-authoring tools, tactile displays, conversational chart exploration, first-person video benchmarks, and context-aware mobile interaction. The recurring design principle is progressive, user-directed grounding rather than one-shot visual descriptions.

topics.name: Reasoning-Model Post-Training
topics.summary: Reasoning models are adapted with verifiable-reward optimization, continuous-time objectives, on-policy delta distillation, answer-independent masking, instruction tuning, and model merging. Results show gains can coexist with capability loss or behavioral drift when the training signal is narrowly specified.

topics.name: Neuro-Symbolic and Verifiable Language Systems
topics.summary: Language models are paired with executable programs, symbolic solvers, structured schemas, academic feedback protocols, and sports-domain tooling. These systems improve auditability and numerical or logical reliability, but still depend on correct premise selection and external checks.

topics.name: Internal Interpretability and Explainable AI
topics.summary: Interpretability work examines attention through statistical scaling, compares decision geometries, decodes verbalizable internal states, and replaces unrealistic image perturbations with photorealistic counterfactuals. The studies prioritize faithful mechanisms and inspectable intermediate behavior over attractive explanations alone.

topics.name: Efficient Language Model Inference
topics.summary: Inference systems reduce cost with adaptive low-bit arithmetic, compiler and hardware co-design, register-resident computation, recurrence, KV-cache compression, speculative verification, and exact or precision-aware caching. CPU, GPU, and diffusion-language experiments show quality can be retained under severe memory limits.

topics.name: Optimization Theory and Neural Training Dynamics
topics.summary: Optimization analyses study adaptive step control, Muon geometry, local-SGD heterogeneity, Hamiltonian sampling, fractional gradients, residual-network stability, and hyperconnection design. Their experiments and bounds distinguish lower training loss or faster computation from improvements that transfer to new data.

topics.name: Knowledge Graphs and Temporal Reasoning
topics.summary: Graph-reasoning systems use schema constraints, adaptive retrieval depth, neural point processes, hop-bounded question generation, and reachability-aware path exploration. The benchmarks stress event order, long-range dependencies, relation compatibility, and uncertain timing rather than static graph lookup.

topics.name: Multi-Agent Learning and Strategic Coordination
topics.summary: Multi-agent studies examine hindsight or on-policy feedback, private-information games, semantic communication, graph memory, and cooperation under resource pressure. Performance depends on selective information exchange and incentive-compatible coordination rather than simply adding more agents.

topics.name: Off-Policy Evaluation and Bandit Decision-Making
topics.summary: Sequential-decision methods address logged feedback, long-horizon covariate imbalance, bursty communication, and graph-path uncertainty with kernel weighting, balance diagnostics, Bayesian exploration, and confidence bounds. The recurring concern is reliable policy selection when outcomes are only partially observed.

topics.name: Time-Series Alignment and Event Analysis
topics.summary: Time-series methods quantify local alignment reliability, parallelize dynamic programming, and attribute multivariate change points or asymmetric peaks. Audio and operational forecasting experiments connect computational savings with more useful detection of localized events and risk-relevant extremes.

topics.name: Physics-Informed System Identification
topics.summary: Sparse regression, neural differential models, and probabilistic physics-informed networks recover dynamics or material properties from noisy, low-resolution, or partially observed measurements. Explicit mechanistic structure improves latent-state estimation and long-horizon prediction in scientific and engineering applications.

topics.name: Recommender Systems and Urban Mobility
topics.summary: Mobility and recommendation studies model feedback loops, online user updates, equilibrium reduction, routing incentives, and fleet competition. Results show that local ranking or route choices can produce system-level effects, so evaluation must include welfare, resilience, and coordinated behavior.

topics.name: Financial Language and Market Analysis
topics.summary: Financial applications combine blockchain activity, social signals, technical indicators, and language-model analysis for sentiment classification and simulated trading. The studies find useful predictive structure but persistent sensitivity to numerical errors, context limits, and changing market regimes.

topics.name: Applied Language Processing and Educational Assessment
topics.summary: Language-processing studies cover scaffolded EFL writing, automated feedback, first-language scoring bias, multilingual vocabulary, log-ratio language identification, crime-domain entities, scientific indexing, and code generation. Corpus-scale evaluations show that proficiency, language background, and domain-specific representation strongly affect results.

topics.name: Synthetic Data and Privacy-Preserving Evaluation
topics.summary: Synthetic cohorts are evaluated for face-recognition benchmarking, medical bias analysis, and membership-information leakage. Findings indicate that subgroup coverage and population construction determine whether generated data preserve rankings, expose disparities, or provide meaningful privacy.

topics.name: Robustness, Noisy Labels, and Domain Shift
topics.summary: Robust-learning studies address black-box attacks, adaptive perturbations, query-specific restoration, medical segmentation shift, noisy human labels, industrial anomalies, and corruption-sensitive training. Across vision and clinical data, explicit quality or shift modeling outperforms assuming that source labels and confidence scores are reliable.

topics.name: Network Anomaly Detection
topics.summary: Network-monitoring pipelines improve intrusion classification with entropy-based traffic variability and Choquet-integral aggregation of redundant features. The experiments emphasize compact representations that retain detection quality while limiting computation and communication overhead.

topics.name: Interactive Visual Analytics
topics.summary: Visual-analytics tools support narrative authoring, coordinated categorical displays, geometric reordering, and natural-language explanations of complex data. Their shared contribution is helping users inspect patterns, sensitivities, and recommendations through interactive evidence rather than static plots.

topics.name: Continual Foundation Model Adaptation
topics.summary: Foundation models are updated through adaptive weight interpolation and in-place tokenizer growth after distribution changes. The methods aim to preserve prior alignment and language coverage while reducing retraining cost and limiting destructive forgetting.

topics.name: Autonomous-Driving Perception and Planning
topics.summary: Autonomous-driving studies combine probabilistic bird's-eye-view perception, causal reasoning about roadwork, and public acceptance evidence. Together they link scene reconstruction and trajectory planning with the social and environmental conditions that affect deployment.

topics.name: Built-Environment Visual Reasoning and Search
topics.summary: Built-environment applications compare model and expert judgments for street-view typology, query semantic city models, and rerank conversational real-estate results. Performance benefits from domain context and human validation, especially when visual categories or user intent are ambiguous.

topics.name: Computational Political Science with Language Models
topics.summary: Political-language studies use coalition simulations, ideological audits of encyclopedic content, and hierarchical stance datasets from short-video conversations. Provenance, multi-judge comparison, and human annotations help separate model-generated narratives from measurable political patterns.

topics.name: Safe and Interpretable Reinforcement Learning
topics.summary: Sequential-control methods combine peak-cost constraints, executable rule extraction, and certificate-based offline learning. Their results show that readable policies and risk guarantees are useful only when edits remain performance-checked and uncertainty is handled explicitly.
